title: Productivity investment with actual output and adoption outcomes
analysis_model: SI-1 Option A design reference PR616 85317167b4001dc027216c1c4e2faf058f0631a3; not runtime authoritative
transmission: Source observation → scoped mechanism → applicability test → decision question; no automatic enterprise pressure
evidenced_consequence: RTI output/hour +0.7% yoy in Q2; real business investment +0.4% qoq in Q3, different periods. No firm-level productivity loss measured.
why_now: Latest growth and policy evidence allows more specific sector investigation.
open_decision_status: UNKNOWN — Which funded asset/process/adoption choice can still change a measured outcome?
counter_evidence: LFS productivity estimate is -0.2%, different method. Investment and output can rise without a missing supplier.
next_salesperson_learning_action: Choose a named sector/enterprise; acquire actual process baseline, adoption, current capex/controls and residual choice.

title: Repricing and financing outcomes across unequal customer cohorts
analysis_model: SI-1 Option A design reference PR616 85317167b4001dc027216c1c4e2faf058f0631a3; not runtime authoritative
transmission: Source observation → scoped mechanism → applicability test → decision question; no automatic enterprise pressure
evidenced_consequence: Different new/stock mortgage and deposit rates and weaker SME survey supply/demand are observed. No named firm funding gap established.
why_now: November policy move is later than September rates and August survey window; obtain next releases before causal attribution.
open_decision_status: UNKNOWN — Which actual cohort and financing/service remedy remain undecided?
counter_evidence: Household real income improved; low demand can explain lending weakness; hedges/current support may suffice.
next_salesperson_learning_action: Obtain current matched-period cohort rates, maturities, outcomes, hedges and existing support before suggesting a financing or service intervention.

title: Operating leverage after delivered improvements

title: Retail deposits and customer value without a funding-crisis narrative
analysis_model: SI-1 Option A design reference PR616 85317167b4001dc027216c1c4e2faf058f0631a3; not runtime authoritative
transmission: Source observation → scoped mechanism → applicability test → decision question; no automatic enterprise pressure
evidenced_consequence: Group deposits+6.3bn YTD; Commercial+9.6bn, Retail-3.7bn and Central Items+0.4bn (0.2bn to0.6bn). Management attributes Retail decline mainly to Q1 savings movements and disciplined pricing; Q3 balances broadly stable. A liability-stock change is not income loss or churn evidence.
why_now: Current Group and segment directions differ and deserve a cohort-specific explanation.
open_decision_status: UNKNOWN — Is there an unresolved retention/service/pricing decision for a particular customer cohort?
counter_evidence: Group funding and NIM improved; management reports Q1 savings movements and disciplined pricing, with Q3 Retail balances broadly stable.
next_salesperson_learning_action: Does the disclosed Q1 savings/pricing explanation fit permitted cohort evidence, did any actual customer outcome worsen, and what decision remains beyond existing pricing/service actions?
